Swing lifecycle

Which part of the move are you investigating?

11 short chapters

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Attention persistence11Market maturity & the method boundary

01Definition

A lifecycle is a working map: discovery, expansion, supply transfer, repricing, then a base or failure.

02Why it matters

The same pause can mean different things before and after major supply transfer.

03What to check

  • What happened before the current range
  • Evidence of demand and ownership changes
  • Conditions that would support or invalidate continuation

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

The stage description changes when the evidence changes.

Dangerous

Every token is forced into a fixed sequence or promised next stage.

05Beginner mistake

Using the same interpretation at every stage.

06Takeaway

Locate the stage. Keep the next outcome conditional.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Expansion is followed by selling and a lower stable range.

  2. 02

    Demand later returns and the range starts being tested from above.

  3. 03

    Continuation is a hypothesis to test, not a scheduled next step.

Go deeper

Continuation and failure are branches, not compulsory destinations. If history, ownership, or current demand is missing, describe the stage as uncertain and record what evidence you need next.
